stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s price slipped 0.5% on the day, leaving it 2.5% below its 52‑week high and still 39.8% above its 52‑week low. The stock is up 22.6% YTD, buoyed by solid month‑over‑month gains. Watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of sustained momentum versus valuation pressure near the top of its range.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft fell 1.6% intraday, now sitting 7.5% under its 52‑week peak while remaining 41.2% above its low. YTD performance is modest at +5.8% with flat weekly and monthly moves. Investors should focus on cloud‑segment growth and any updates to its AI roadmap as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA edged up 0.6% but remains 9.8% shy of its 52‑week high, still 28.7% above its low after a 12.6% YTD rise. The recent weekly and monthly declines suggest short‑term profit‑taking. Key watch: the company’s next GPU launch timeline and AI demand trends could dictate direction.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet slipped 1.3% on the day, now 14.2% below its 52‑week high yet 46.2% above its low, with a 9.7% YTD gain. Weekly momentum is modestly positive while the month is flat. Investors should monitor ad‑tech revenue trends and any regulatory developments as the next driver.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon dropped 2.0% today, trading 12.5% under its 52‑week high and 25.0% above its low, with a 9.7% YTD increase despite recent declines across all short‑term frames. The stock’s weakness reflects pressure on its retail margins. Watch the upcoming earnings report for insight into cost‑control measures and growth in its cloud segment.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta rose 0.7% on the day, still 13.8% below its 52‑week high but 27.6% above its low, after a strong 13.6% monthly gain and a 9.3% weekly surge. YTD growth is modest at 3.2%. The next catalyst is the rollout of AI‑enhanced ad products and user‑engagement metrics.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla slipped 0.7% and remains 27.2% below its 52‑week high, though it is 19.5% above its low after a 4.2% monthly gain. The stock is down 18.6% YTD, reflecting broader market weakness. Watch production updates from its new factories and any guidance on pricing or margin pressure.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom fell 1.6% and is now 29.4% under its 52‑week high, barely above its low at +15.8%, with a slight YTD decline of 2.0%. Weekly and monthly moves are sharply negative. Investors should keep an eye on its semiconductor demand outlook and upcoming dividend announcements.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD jumped 2.2% intraday, still 13.2% below its 52‑week high but a massive 220.4% above its low, after a 125.6% YTD surge. Weekly and monthly performance is near flat, indicating a consolidation phase. The next key factor is the launch schedule for its next‑gen GPUs and server chip adoption rates.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 3.1% on the day and is down 13.6% week‑to‑date, sitting 56.7% below its 52‑week high and still 22.1% above its lows, indicating a deep pull‑back from peak valuations. The recent earnings miss and weaker cloud guidance keep pressure on the stock. Investors should watch the next quarterly guidance and any signs of turnaround in its cloud services revenue.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce rallied 30.3% over the past month and is now just 3.5% shy of its 52‑week high, while still 70.3% above its low, reflecting a strong recovery after its earlier slowdown. Momentum is supported by recent AI‑driven product launches and better‑than‑expected earnings. The key catalyst to monitor is the impact of its AI strategy on subscription growth and margin expansion in the coming quarters.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan edged up 0.7% today, trading 3.5% below its 52‑week high and 25.8% above its low, with YTD gains near 10%. The bank remains resilient amid modest weekly volatility, buoyed by solid net interest income. Investors should focus on upcoming Fed policy signals and the bank’s loan‑loss provisions as they could sway earnings momentum.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America is marginally higher today, still 7.7% under its 52‑week peak but 28.7% above its trough, delivering a 8.1% YTD gain. Recent earnings beat and higher interest‑rate environment have supported the stock, though weekly weakness persists. The next watch point is the bank’s credit‑quality trends and any shifts in net interest margin expectations.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa ticked up 0.1% and remains near its 52‑week high, down just 2.2% while up 27.6% from its low, delivering a 9.1% YTD rise. Transaction volumes are holding steady, but the stock is sensitive to consumer‑spending trends. Investors should keep an eye on quarterly volume growth and any regulatory developments affecting interchange fees.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard is marginally down 0.2% but sits 4.4% below its 52‑week high and 21.8% above its low, with a modest 2.3% YTD gain. The firm’s earnings have been stable, yet growth is slowing as payment volumes normalize. The key metric to watch is the pace of international expansion and the impact of emerging‑market competition on fee income.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix fell 3% on the day, trading 37.2% below its 52‑week high yet still 15.2% above its low, with a 14.4% YTD decline. Subscriber growth has stalled, and the recent price cut has pressured margins. The next inflection point is the upcoming earnings report, particularly churn rates and the performance of its ad‑supported tier.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly slipped 0.2% but remains 11.3% under its 52‑week high while soaring 60% above its low, posting a 5.7% YTD gain. Strong pipeline momentum continues to drive the stock despite a modest monthly dip. Investors should monitor the FDA review timeline for its late‑stage diabetes candidates and any pricing pressure on its blockbuster drugs.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth dropped 2% today, now 13.3% below its 52‑week high but 46.9% above its low, with a solid 14% YTD rise. The health‑insurer’s earnings beat has been tempered by slower enrollment growth. The critical watch item is the next enrollment data and potential regulatory changes affecting Medicare Advantage margins.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has nudged up 0.3% today, holding 4.0% below its 52‑week high and still 56.9% above its low, with a solid 30.9% YTD gain. The modest daily rise follows a slight weekly dip, suggesting the stock is consolidating near the top of its range. Investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for clues on whether the upward momentum can be sustained.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart slipped 0.9% on the day, now sitting 19.3% under its 52‑week high but only 8.3% above its low, with a modest 3.5% YTD decline. The recent weekly gain masks a broader downtrend over the month. Key focus will be the retailer’s same‑store sales trends and any updates to its low‑price strategy.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco fell 1.9% today, trading 17.5% below its 52‑week peak while still 6.5% above its low, and is up 5.9% YTD. The stock has been pressured across the week and month, indicating a possible short‑term pullback. Watch membership renewal trends and any guidance on inventory costs for next‑move signals.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot dropped 1.7% on the day, now 25.5% off its 52‑week high and just 4.2% above its low, with a 9.7% YTD decline. The broader downtrend across the week and month suggests the stock is testing support near its low. Investors should monitor housing market data and the company’s upcoming earnings for a potential turning point.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil rose 2.6% today, sitting essentially at its 52‑week high and 57.5% above its low, with a strong 40.8% YTD rally. The daily gain adds to a solid weekly and monthly advance, reflecting bullish energy pricing. The next catalyst is likely crude‑oil price movements and the company’s capital‑allocation plan announced at earnings.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola slipped 0.1% today, now 3.0% below its 52‑week high and 38.7% above its low, with a robust 30.8% YTD increase. The stock’s slight daily dip follows modest weekly and monthly gains, indicating steady momentum near the top of its range. Watch for the upcoming earnings report and any updates on pricing power amid input cost pressures.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney fell 2.0% on the day, trading 7.5% under its 52‑week high and 16.0% above its low, with a 4.1% YTD decline. The stock’s mixed weekly gain and slight monthly dip suggest volatility around its recent lows. Investors should focus on the streaming subscriber growth and the rollout of the new park attractions as near‑term drivers.
